meta.title: MCP Question Bank — Chapter 9: MCP Inspector
meta.revision: v2.1 (curated 2026-09-12, 200 items, verified against the 2026-07-28 specification)

questions.question: You want to inspect a colleague's config file without the Inspector ever modifying it. Which flag, and what happens if the file is missing?

options.text: --catalog with --read-only, and a missing file is an error
--config: it is writable but backed up first, and a missing file is seeded
--config: it is never written or seeded, and a missing file is an error
--catalog: it is read-only by default, and a missing file is created empty

questions.explanation: --config is served as-is: never written, seeded or migrated, and it errors if the file does not exist. --catalog is the writable working set, defaulting to ~/.mcp-inspector/mcp.json, created and seeded when missing. The two are mutually exclusive.

questions.question: A CI job runs the Inspector CLI against a protected server and exits with code 3. What happened, and which flag makes this deterministic?

options.text: Authentication is required; --stored-auth-only fails fast instead of waiting
The server was unreachable; --connect-timeout shortens how long it waits
A tool returned isError: true; --format json makes the failure parseable
Usage was wrong; --help prints the flags that this client accepts

questions.explanation: Exit 3 means the server requires authentication (401/403, WWW-Authenticate, OAuth). --stored-auth-only never starts interactive OAuth and never opens a browser: it uses a stored token if present and otherwise fails immediately with auth_required. 4 is unreachable, 5 is a tool error, 1 is usage.

questions.question: Why must the Inspector's OAuth callback URL stay on loopback, and what is the default?

options.text: The authorization server requires a registered public URL; default https://localhost:6276
The code arrives over plaintext http, so only loopback is accepted; default port 6276
Browsers block cross-origin redirects, so only localhost works; default port 6274
It need not be loopback: --callback-url accepts any host reachable by the browser

questions.explanation: The local callback listener receives the authorization code over plaintext http, so any non-loopback host is rejected and there is no flag to override it. The default is http://127.0.0.1:6276/oauth/callback; 6274 is the web UI port.

questions.question: A catalog entry omits protocolEra and modernLogLevel. Which defaults apply?

options.text: protocolEra modern, modernLogLevel off unless the server advertises logging
protocolEra auto-detected per connection, modernLogLevel debug
protocolEra modern, modernLogLevel info
protocolEra legacy, modernLogLevel debug

questions.explanation: Per-server settings default to protocolEra legacy and modernLogLevel debug, and fields equal to their default are omitted when the Inspector writes the catalog back, keeping diffs small.

questions.question: A fresh catalog is created by the CLI and by the web client. How do the two differ?

options.text: The CLI seeds two sample servers; the web client starts empty so nothing is created silently
Both seed the same two sample servers, so sessions are reproducible
The web client seeds two sample servers; the CLI and TUI seed an empty mcpServers object
Neither seeds anything: seeding only happens when --seed is passed

questions.explanation: Seeding happens only when the file does not exist. The web backend seeds a filesystem and an everything server so a first launch has something to connect to, while the CLI and TUI, being non-interactive or list-driven, seed { "mcpServers": {} }.

questions.question: A pipeline probes a tool with --app-info. The tool name is misspelled. Which exit code distinguishes that from 'the tool has no MCP App'?

options.text: 4 for a missing tool, 0 for a tool with no app
1 for a missing tool, 2 for a tool with no app
2 for a missing tool, 5 for a tool with no app
5 for a missing tool, 2 for a tool with no app

questions.explanation: A tool with an app exits 0, one with no app exits 2, and a missing tool exits 5, so a typo is not mistaken for 'no app'. Every non-zero exit also writes a single JSON error line to stderr.

questions.question: Why does the documentation single out combining DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH with DANGEROUSLY_BIND_ALL_INTERFACES?

options.text: The combination is rejected at startup, so the Inspector will not run at all
The backend spawns processes and holds OAuth tokens, so anyone who can reach it can drive it
Omitting auth resets the catalog, letting any remote user overwrite the stored server definitions
Binding all interfaces disables TLS, exposing tokens on the wire

questions.explanation: Either flag alone is a development convenience; together they expose an unauthenticated service that spawns processes and holds tokens to the whole network. The documentation warns never to combine them rather than blocking it.

questions.question: You add a modern-only server to a fresh Inspector catalog entry and every request fails before reaching your handler. What is the likely cause?

options.text: protocolEra was left at its default of legacy, so the Inspector speaks the old revision
The catalog was seeded read-only, so the Inspector cannot record the new connection at all
modernLogLevel defaults to debug, so the server rejects the noisy log level
The Inspector defaults to port 6276, which is reserved for the OAuth callback

questions.explanation: protocolEra defaults to legacy, so an entry that omits it talks to a modern-only server in the wrong dialect and fails at the transport. modernLogLevel defaults to debug and is harmless; 6274 is the web UI and 6276 the loopback OAuth callback.
